content:
CNN conservative pundit Scott Jennings’ defense of Donald Trump’s sharing of a new, apparently AI-generated image — which has been condemned as “disgusting” — prompted a sharp rebuke from “NewsNight” guest host Elie Honig on Monday.

Trump posted online an image celebrating Nvidia’s reinstatement of Jensen Huang as its CEO and president, after he resigned only days ago after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Trump’s post depicted Huang in place of him following the 2024 assassination attempt against the president in Butler, Pennsylvania, and holding up a red bra.

Honig asked the Trump-loving and Trump-endorsed Jennings, who has been named as a potential future White House press secretary, to explain the image.

“I get the reference to Butler, Pennsylvania here, but what the hell is up with the red bra? What does that mean? Interpret for us,” he said.

Jennings responded: “Do you actually need me to tell you what it means or are you just asking me? Do you really need me to spell it out for you? I mean, you could just lighten up a little and chuckle. I mean, it’s a meme.”

Honig countered by asking Jennings if he knew who Corey Comperatore was, referring to the former volunteer firefighter chief killed during the assassination attempt.

“He’s the man who was killed at Butler,” Jennings replied.

Honig asked whether Jennings thought that was funny and whether he believed Comperatore’s family would be “laughing at that image with the bra, ‘haha.’”

Jennings argued that Comperatore’s family “is very grateful for how the president has interacted with them,” before asking Honig if he was “seriously telling me that you don’t see a little bit of humor in this on a day like today.”

“I don’t know, I don’t think Corey Comperatore’s family,” Honig began, before Jennings interrupted.

“I mean, the president the president was shot. Does he not have the right to make light of his own situation?” he added.

Honig then brought the discussion to a close.
